newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb kills at least 300 on India train - police.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills at least 300 on India train - police.

text.p: At least 300 people were believed killed when a bomb ripped through a packed express train carrying New Year holiday travellers in remote northeastern India, police said on Tuesday.
Three carriages were destroyed in the blast after the train had left Kokrajhar station in Assam state for Delhi at around 7 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Monday, they said.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, which authorities blamed on Bodo tribal guerrillas who have waged a violent separatist struggle for nearly a decade.
"Bodo guerrillas blew up three coaches of a passenger train killing at least 300 people at Sensapani railway station," a senior police official in Assam's capital Guwahati told Reuters.
He said militants had used a remote-controlled device to blow up the Delhi-bound Brahmaputra Mail, an express train named after the sacred river that flows through India's northeast.
Regional railway spokesman J.D. Goswami told Reuters in Guwahati that 30 bodies had been recovered from the mangled wreckage.
He said 42 injured passengers had been moved to a hospital in West Bengal state, 50 km (30 miles) to the south.
But darkness hampered rescue work and made it impossible to know how many people had died although local railway officials said the final death count was expected to be much higher.
The Press Trust of India news agency quoted officials as saying the death toll was at least 300.
If police fears were realised, it would make the attack the second most devastating guerrilla action on record.
In June 1985, Sikh extremists were blamed for a bomb on an Air India Boeing 747 which crashed into the sea off Ireland, killing 329 people.
In December 1988, 270 died when a bomb destroyed a Pan American Boeing 747 over the Scottish town of Lockerbie.

Around 1,000 people were travelling on the train, which officials said had about 15 carriages, each one crammed with 75 to 100 people. Most of the passengers were believed to be holiday-makers heading for Delhi to celebrate the New Year.
Sensapani is 200 km (125 miles) west of Guwahati, hub of the oil-producing and tea-rich state, seven km (four miles) west of Kokrajhar, a centre of Bodo separatist activity.
The Bodos are one of many indigenous tribes in hilly northeastern India and among dozens of groups waging violent separatist campaigns across the country.
The animist Bodos have been demanding a separate tribal state north of the Brahmaputra river since the early 1980s, and their campaign took a violent turn at the end of the decade.
At least 1,000 had died in violence related to the Bodo struggle for independence, United News of India said.

One of the coaches torn apart by the blast was an air-conditioned carriage with reserved seats. Another was for passengers without reservations and was thought to be carrying far more than its capacity.
The third carriage was a restaurant car, and railway officials said an explosion of cooking gas cylinders could have caused more deaths.
Police and residents of Kokrajhar town said they heard two explosions.
A police and medical team reached the site of the devastation in darkness around midnight (1830 GMT) and had to set up emergency lighting before rescue operations could resume.
Sixteen survivors walked three km (two miles) to the next station at Fakiragram.
The attack came a day after Bodo guerrillas blew up a road bridge that formed the main link between India's northeast regions and the rest of the country, injuring seven people.

Activists representing Bodo tribesmen living north of the Brahmaputra river want a homeland within India in the state of Assam, but an extremist fringe, the Bodoland Army, has been fighting for a separate nation since 1989.
Bodo guerrillas have carried out ambushes, kidnappings and attacked railway lines in the past.
Police said none of the several guerrillas groups operating in Assam had claimed responsibility for the blast.
More than 5,000 people have been killed in ethnic and separatist violence in Assam during the last three years.
